settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: A fixed '.json' suffix is appended, constraining reachable targets to *.json paths.
An 'en' fallback is appended in some code paths, which may mask crafted values.
servlet.getModule(modname) returning null for an unknown module could throw or short-circuit before path use, constraining the module parameter.
candidates.description: In the read range, LoadLanguageCommand derives a filesystem path for a translation file from HTTP request parameters. doPost/doGet path handling reads request.getParameter("module") (defaulting to "core") and request.getParameterValues("lang"), then loadLanguage builds a File by concatenating the module's path with a fixed "langs" directory segment and the lang value plus a ".json" suffix, and returns the file content as JSON. No sanitization of the lang value (or module name) is visible in the read range, so a value containing path separators or ".." could in principle escape the intended langs directory. LoadLanguageCommand also exposes doGet delegating to doPost, so the value can be supplied via query string. This is flagged as a candidate only; the exact string construction and any validation performed outside the read range were not verified.
missing_evidence: No test or filter stripping path separators from lang/module was observed in the read range.
The precise assembly of the file path (which lines append 'langs' and '.json') was inferred from the read span but not verified against every concatenation.
Whether the servlet container normalizes the query value before getParameter was not verified.
preconditions: Attacker can reach the /command/ dispatch path (the servlet dispatch code read rejects non-/command/ paths but no authentication was observed in the read range).
A 'lang' value containing path separators or traversal sequences is accepted by the null/empty check.
The resulting file exists and contains parseable JSON so its content is returned.
candidates.title: Potential path traversal in LoadLanguageCommand via unvalidated 'module' and 'lang' parameters

counter_evidence: A connection timeout is reported to be set in the read span, bounding hang time but not preventing SSRF.
The fetched content is stored as a project, so reading back exfiltrated data may require an additional capability.
candidates.description: In the read range, ImportProjectCommand reads a multipart form field named "url" and, when non-empty, passes it to an internal import-URL routine that constructs a URL, opens a connection, connects, obtains an input stream and streams the response into the project import. No validation of the URL against private/internal address ranges, localhost, or non-HTTP schemes is visible in the read range. This allows the server to be induced to fetch an attacker-chosen resource and import it as project data, i.e. a server-side request forgery candidate. Flagged as a candidate; the exact openConnection/streaming lines fall in the 134-163 portion of the read span and were not individually re-verified.
missing_evidence: No scheme/allow-list check was observed between the parameter value and openConnection in the read range.
Whether an upstream proxy or servlet filter restricts outbound URLs was not verified.
Exact line-by-line confirmation of the connection/IO code within the read span.
preconditions: Attacker can POST a multipart/form-data request to the import-project command path.
The supplied URL is resolvable from the server host.
candidates.title: Potential SSRF in ImportProjectCommand via 'url' form field
